extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers seeking an encyclopedic biography of Gerald Posner
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style encyclopedic biography of an investigative journalist and author (Gerald Posner). The page combines career overview, book-by-book reception, and controversies — from which evaluative criteria for investigative nonfiction and biographical entries can be inferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meticulous research
rubrics_metrics.description: Works praised as 'meticulous' or 'meticulously researched' — research must be thorough and exhaustive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple reviews describe Posner's books (e.g., Case Closed) as 'meticulous' research; good investigative nonfiction should demonstrate deep documentary digging, comprehensive review of prior literature, and corroboration across many sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of primary/exclusive sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain and use primary documents and exclusive materials (e.g., 'obtained exclusive access to 5,000 pages of Mengele's diaries and personal papers').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary-source access (archives, diaries, witness statements) strengthens a work's authority; cite and explain provenance of such materials when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritativeness / definitive treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Being described as 'definitive' or 'authoritative' — the book should offer comprehensive and convincing coverage of its subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depth, breadth, and synthesis that resolve outstanding questions or reframe debates can make a work authoritative; ensure claims are well-supported and caveated where uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unbiased / balanced exploration of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting an 'unbiased in its exploration of every claim' approach — fairly examine competing views and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and present contrary evidence, interrogate own conclusions, and avoid partisan or one-sided treatment; reviewers (e.g., Anthony Lewis) praised such balance in Posner's work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readable narrative and clear prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative flow and readability ('written in a penetrating, lucid style', 'readable book') are valued alongside research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine rigorous reporting with clear, engaging prose; avoid unnecessary jargon or over-dramatization while keeping narrative momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual accuracy and avoidance of errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'factual errors' and 'inaccuracies' that critics say can 'suffuse' a work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact-check all claims; verify dates, names, and quotations; systematic editorial fact-checking minimizes the risk of large-scale factual mistakes that undermine credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful quoting and correct attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'misquoting,' 'misattributed quotes,' or 'apparently altered or misattributed quotes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep clear records of interviews and sources, preserve exact wording, and provide accurate attribution; misquoting is a serious defect and can catalyze reputational harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper sourcing and citation transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide documentation (notes, appendices, footnotes) and be transparent about sources and methods ('assiduously digs into the business practices', 'meticulous footnotes' implied).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include citations and, where appropriate, appendices listing archival materials or interview dates; transparency allows readers and reviewers to audit claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of plagiarism and rigorous source management
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not appropriate others' material — Poynter's Roy Peter Clark: 'This constitutes plagiarism by any definition I can think of.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain careful note-taking practices, clearly distinguish quoted material from paraphrase in research files, provide attribution for paraphrase and direct quotes, and uphold publication ethics to avoid plagiarism allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to detected errors (corrections/amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: When significant errors are identified, rectify them in subsequent editions (Posner amended the paperback of God's Bankers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue corrections, errata, or revised editions when legitimate errors are found; document what changed and why to restore trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous fieldwork and first-hand reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct in-person research and interviews when necessary ('traveled ... to conduct in-person research with drug traffickers', obtained witness statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-hand reporting (interviews, site visits, witness statements) bolsters claims; employ standard safeguards for source protection and corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution about making expert claims beyond one's qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid presenting technical or psychological evaluations for which the author lacks expertise (critique that Posner 'is not qualified to give' a psychological evaluation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If making specialized assessments (medical, psychological, scientific), consult or cite qualified experts and make limitations of one’s expertise explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support novel or controversial conclusions with strong evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: When advancing contentious theses (e.g., Oswald acted alone), provide exhaustive evidence and anticipate scholarly critique ('continued to generate widely divergent views').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document chain of evidence, cite primary sources, and engage with opposing scholarship; expect and address detailed counterarguments to controversial claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid manipulating public records or online entries about the author
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not 'scrub' or alter public encyclopedia entries to conceal controversies (evidence indicated Posner 'scrubbed' elements from his Wikipedia page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain transparency about controversies; editing related public pages for self-promotion or concealment is unethical and risks further reputational damage.
